sections.skill: Plan around usage limits and response time

questions.prompt: What is a usage limit?

choices.text: A cap on how much you can use a tool
A rule that says how fast you must type when you send a message to the tool

questions.correct_answer: A cap on how much you can use a tool
questions.intro: Two practical limits shape how you use AI tools. USAGE LIMITS cap how much you can do: a number of messages per day or hour, a maximum file size, or a spending cap. LATENCY is the waiting time between sending a request and getting the answer; larger models, longer answers and busy times usually mean longer waits. Plan around both: do heavy work early instead of right before a deadline, keep a backup plan if you hit a limit, and for tasks needing quick replies, such as live chat, choose faster options even if they are slightly less capable.

sections.skill: Compare usage limits with a library's borrowing rules

questions.prompt: A 5-book borrowing cap is like what?
questions.correct_answer: A usage limit
questions.intro: A library might let you borrow 5 books at a time, and popular books may have a waiting list. If you need books for a project due Friday, you go early in the week, not Thursday night. AI tools are similar: limits are like the borrowing cap, and latency is like waiting for a book that others are reading. Planning ahead avoids being stuck.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Build resilience against changing limits and outages

questions.prompt: A free plan's limit was lowered without much notice. What does this show?

choices.text: That limits are fixed by law

questions.correct_answer: Limits can change
questions.intro: Limits can change without much notice, especially on free plans, and busy periods may slow responses or block requests temporarily. Automations that call a tool many times can hit rate limits (how many requests per minute are allowed) and fail partway; design them to wait and retry slowly. For important deadlines, do not depend on one tool always being available. Save your work as you go so a limit or outage does not erase progress.
